articles.title: Royals In Market For Right-Handed Hitting Outfielder
body: The Royals are looking for a right-handed hitting outfielder, general manager J.J. Picollo told reporters at the GM Meetings this week (link via ESPN’s Jesse Rogers). The GM added that an acquisition would ideally be capable of playing center field on at least a part-time basis.

That’s essentially the role Lane Thomas played for K.C. this year. They picked him up on a one-year, $5.25MM free agent contract last offseason. Thomas played reasonably well for a half-season, batting.232/.326/.393 across 97 games. He started 72 contests in the outfield, 52 of them up the middle. They traded him to Atlanta at the deadline for a pair of minor league pitchers and to dump what remained of Bailey Falter’s arbitration salary.

Thomas didn’t play particularly well for the Braves. He’s back on the market and might be available even more cheaply than he was a year ago if the Royals wanted to reengage. Tyrone Taylor, Myles Straw, Jake Meyers and Victor Robles are other possibilities as fourth/fifth outfield types. If the Royals wanted a potential everyday center fielder, Luis Robert Jr. is the top right-handed hitter on the free agent market.

articles.title: The Best Fits For Tarik Skubal
body: The spotlight is on Tarik Skubal, who is the top free agent of the offseason. He is one of the best pitchers alive right now. He has a 2.64 earned run average over the past four seasons. His 30.1% strikeout rate and 4.8% walk rate in that time are both elite figures. His 44.6% ground ball rate in that span isn’t quite as gaudy but is still better than average. He won the American League Cy Young in both 2024 and 2025.

His 2026 was interrupted by an elbow surgery but he still managed to post a 2.72 ERA over 26 starts, plus two more postseason starts. He was traded midseason, making him ineligible for a qualifying offer. Even if he did have the QO, it would be a minor consideration for a player this talented, but the lack of QO only helps.

Skubal is the best classic, prime-aged starter to hit the market in years. Shohei Ohtani was obviously a special case as a two-way player. In terms of pure pitchers, it’s expected that Skubal’s contract will set new benchmarks in terms of guarantee or average annual value or both. The record in the former category is Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325MM deal with the Dodgers. In the latter camp, both Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander got AAVs of $43.33MM late in their careers.

articles.title: Angels, Tyler Heineman Avoid Arbitration
body: The Angels announced that they have signed catcher Tyler Heineman to a one-year deal for the 2027 season worth $1.2375MM. They also re-signed left-hander Sammy Peralta via a minor league contract with an invitation to spring training.

Heineman, 36 in June, is a journeyman catcher. He has played for the Marlins, Giants, Blue Jays, Pirates, Red Sox and Angels in his career. He had a really nice season with the Jays in 2025, backing up Alejandro Kirk. Heineman hit.289/.361/.416 in 174 plate appearances. He also got strong grades for his work behind the plate. FanGraphs credited him with 2.1 wins above replacement. He got into a couple of postseason games as the Jays made a World Series run.

Though he was 34 years old, he qualified for arbitration for the first time after that season. The Jays tendered him a contract for his age-35 season and the two sides avoided a hearing by agreeing to a salary of $1.2375. Unfortunately, he couldn’t carry things over into 2026. While Kirk was on the injured list, the Jays called up Brandon Valenzuela to share the catching duties with Heineman. Valenzuela played well as Heineman struggled. Heineman is out of options so he was designated for assignment when Kirk came off the IL.

articles.title: Cardinals Reportedly Turned Away Trade Interest In Burleson, Winn
body: The Cardinals are fielding calls on a lot of players on their roster. Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports that the Cards have received interested in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, shortstop Masyn Winn and first baseman Alec Burleson, though Goold notes that the club quickly turned away the interest in both Winn and Burleson.

It’s not surprising that the phone would ring. The Cardinals have been in seller mode for a while. Last offseason, they traded away Sonny Gray, Nolan Arenado, Willson Contreras and Brendan Donovan to clear payroll and make room for younger players. At this year’s deadline, they traded away Dustin May, JoJo Romero and Lars Nootbaar. Those pitchers were all impending free agents while each position player was under club control through at least 2027.

With all that selling, it’s understandable that clubs with needs would keep the lines open. The Cards seem to be planning for 2027 to be another evaluation year, so players nearing free agency would be logical trade candidates.

Burleson is under club control through 2028. The Cards could emerge as legitimate contenders in that time frame but it’s unclear how aggressively they plan to tackle things in that window. He just hit 26 home runs this year and slashed.279/.343/.473, so now would be a good time to sell high.

articles.title: Blue Jays Rumors: Valenzuela, Clement, Smith, Schneider, Pitching
body: The hot stove is warming up. The Blue Jays haven’t made a big move yet but the buzz on them continues to be that they’re exploring just about everything. Mitch Bannon of The Athletic as well as Ben-Nicholson Smith and Shi Davidi of Sportsnet have details on some of the various things that are up in the air with the club.

Bannon notes that the Jays are getting some trade interest in catcher Brandon Valenzuela. Bannon doesn’t specify which clubs are calling but notes that the Reds have had previous interest. Valenzuela had an encouraging debut this year, getting into 91 games for the Jays. He made 271 plate appearances and hit.222/.307/.372. That translates to a 93 wRC+, indicating he was 7% worse than the league average hitter. Catchers are usually 10 to 12% below par, so that’s actually decent production, especially for a backup. Valenzuela also received strong grades for his glovework. FanGraphs credited him with 2.1 wins above replacement.

The Jays could certainly keep Valenzuela as backup to Alejandro Kirk. However, if some other club considers him to be a viable everyday catcher and is willing to pay for him accordingly in terms of a trade return, it could be worth Toronto’s while. In theory, the Jays could flip Valenzuela for a bat or an arm or a package of players and then turn to free agency to find a backup for Kirk.

articles.title: Cubs Notes: Ramirez, Kelly, Hoyer, Staffing
body: The Cubs have two spots to fill in the outfield alongside newly minted NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong with Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki heading to free agency. The internal replacements include Pedro Ramirez, Matt Shaw, and Kevin Alcantara. Ramirez could be the leader in the clubhouse based on recent comments from GM Carter Hawkins.

The lead exec praised Ramirez’ athleticism and work ethic, factors that could help him transition into a more versatile role, as relayed by Meghan Montemurro of the Chicago Tribune. The 22-year-old primarily played second and third base in the minors, but played some first base and left field after his big-league promotion.

“There’s a risk to going with some unproven guys, but that allows you maybe to get some more proven guys in other spots,” Hawkins said. “I don’t think there’s one path that we necessarily would cross out at this juncture.”

Ramirez forced his way to the majors by hitting.312 with nine homers and 19 steals in 43 games at Triple-A. He held his own in his first taste of the highest level, slashing.261/.321/.402 across 266 plate appearances. Ramirez added six homers and nine steals. The thefts have always been a part of his profile, but the power was a big addition in 2026. He’d totaled 25 homers in four pro seasons before popping 15 this year.

articles.title: Front Office Subscriber Chat Transcript
body: Good afternoon, hope all is well! Busy week for us so I’m going to keep this one close to an hour, let’s get it going MarlinsMan
I have a feeling the Marlins may reel someone in… what other dark horse FA could land there? Seems as if the Marlins are interested in a lot of people. Anthony Franco
They do seem to be in on LH relievers so I could see Vesia or Soto there, think there’s an argument for Ty France to push Stowers back to LF Carlton

Only three clubs have made significant signings with the GM meetings behind us. It doesn’t seem like the Skubal mega overpay sweepstakes should have any effect on the vast majority of the remaining clubs, so what’s the hold up? I thought the looming lockout would cause most teams to make preemptive moves. Anthony Franco

It’s just early. The biggest move in the last lockout year before the QO decision date was Andrew Heaney signing for $8.5M. We’ve already had three signings more significant than that with a much weaker FA class Please
Give me one good reason why I should think the lockout will end before the start of spring training Anthony Franco

Before Spring Training would usually start in mid-February? I’ve got nothing, don’t think it’s happening They’ll need some kind of warm-up period and eventually you get to a point where you can no longer dither while still leaving a three week window for camp and the rest of the offseason while still playing 162 And if you don’t get a deal done by then, everyone loses money and negotiations get more difficult because you also need to divide that lost revenue HitsLikeRays

articles.title: Cubs, White Sox, Padres Among Teams Interested In Kaima Taira
body: Right-hander Kaima Taira, star for the Seibu Lions of Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball, is drawing widespread interest after being posted for major league clubs. Bruce Levine of 670 The Score in Chicago reports that both the Cubs and White Sox have “strong” interest in Taira. They were both planning to meet with agent Scott Boras this week, though the Boras Corporation of course represents a large number of this winter’s free agents beyond just Taira. Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune writes that while the Padres have some level of interest in all three NPB stars who were posted this winter — slugger Teruaki Sato and righty Hiromi Itoh being the others — the Friars seem particularly focused on Taira.

The Blue Jays were known to have scouted Taira extensively this past season and have carried their interest into the offseason, per Sportsnet’s Shi Davidi. Toronto has done “lots of background work” on Taira, per the report. Davidi adds that Taira isn’t traveling to North America to meet with interested clubs in person but is conducting frequent Zoom calls with teams major league clubs. That presumably includes Toronto, though it’s not clear whether the two parties have formally spoken or are still lining up a time to do so. The Giants also have some interest in Taira and have discussed him internally, according to John Shea of the San Francisco Standard.

articles.title: Tigers Interested In Shota Imanaga
body: The Tigers entered the offseason in search of help in the rotation and the bullpen. They’ve already addressed the latter, adding former Reds closer Emilio Pagan this week. As far as starting pitching, Jon Morosi of MLB Network reports that left-hander Shota Imanaga is among the free agents the club is interested in.

Imanaga hit free agency last winter but ultimately stayed with the Cubs after accepting the qualifying offer. The 33-year-old is back on the market this offseason and won’t have the QO attached to him this time around. Imanaga put together 32 starts of a 3.77 ERA with nearly a strikeout per inning in 2026. He tossed a career-high 174 1/3 innings as basically the only Cubs starter to stay healthy all year.

Homers are the big issue for Imanaga. He’s a flyball pitcher with middling strikeout stuff. When the wind was blowing in at Wrigley Field, he was an elite starter. When it was blowing out, the long balls came in bunches. Only Phillies righty Aaron Nola (37) gave up more home runs than Imanaga (35) in 2026.

Comerica Park would be an upgrade for Imanaga. Statcast’s Park Factors ranked it 14th for home runs over the past three seasons. Wrigley Field comes in at No. 8 on the leaderboard. For right-handed power, there was basically no difference. Chicago ranked 11th and Detroit ranked 12th for righty homers.

articles.title: Red Sox To Sign Jake Bauers
body: The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers are in agreement on a four-year, $58MM contract, reports ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The VC Sports Group client received a $23.15MM qualifying offer from the Brewers but will turn that down and head to Boston on a lucrative multi-year contract.

Due in no small part to his postseason heroics, Bauers’ story is well known by now. The 31-year-old former top prospect was on the cusp of retirement after seemingly flaming out in the majors. He’d called his agent and informed him of the decision but changed course just days later when his wife learned she was pregnant with their second child and wouldn’t be going back to work — and securing health insurance — as they’d planned. Bauers signed back with the Brewers on a minor league deal ahead of the 2025 season and made the club. Bauers struggled for much of the season and looked like a DFA or non-tender candidate until a massive September saved his roster spot.

That September surge proved to be a portent for a full-fledged breakout. Bauers wasn’t just the Brewers’ best hitter and the eventual NLCS MVP in 2026 — he was one of the best hitters in the entire sport. Dating back to early September of 2025, Bauers has taken 631 regular season plate appearances and mashed at a.276/.396/.494 pace with 28 homers and a 16% walk rate. His 26.1% strikeout rate is too high, but for a player with this type of patience and power output, that’s a more than worthwhile trade-off.

articles.title: Marlins Interested In Patrick Sandoval
body: The Marlins have shown interest in free agent lefty Patrick Sandoval, reports Kevin Barral of Fish On First.

Miami’s rotation has three arms locked into rotation spots: Sandy Alcantara, Eury Pérez and Max Meyer. The final two spots, at present, are filled by swingmen Janson Junk, Ryan Gusto and Tyler Phillips. Top prospects Thomas White and Robby Snelling are effectively ready for big league looks — at least once they’re healthy. Snelling underwent UCL surgery last May just a few starts into his promising young career. White’s season ended in June after he suffered a capsule sprain in his left shoulder.

Meyer and Pérez both missed time due to injuries in 2026 as well. Given the level of injury risk and lack of back-end stability in the Miami rotation, adding some reinforcements is a natural goal. Sandoval, 30, is coming off a lackluster performance in his first season back from Tommy John surgery. He pitched in 15 games (13 of them starts) and tossed 70 1/3 innings with a 5.12 ERA, 22.7% strikeout rate, 10% walk rate and 37.8% ground-ball rate.

articles.title: Twins Promote Jonas Lovin To Assistant Pitching Coach
body: Twins general manager Jeremy Zoll told reporters this week that Jonas Lovin was promoted to the big-league staff. He’ll serve as an assistant to new pitching coach Brian Reith. Lovin has been a minor league pitching coach in Minnesota’s system for the past three seasons.

The Twins moved on from pitching coach Pete Maki and assistant Luis Ramirez at the end of this past season. Reith was hired last month, and the club was expected to find a Ramirez replacement to work with him. Bullpen coach LaTroy Hawkins remains on the staff.

“Jonas has made a huge impact on our minor-league pitching programs and development of our young pitching prospects,” Zoll told reporters, including Dan Hayes of The Athletic. “He has fantastic relationships with our young pitchers and complements Brian and LaTroy’s skill sets in ways that allow us to build a pitching coach group that will be able to serve all of our players’ individual needs on a daily basis.”

Lovin made the jump from the college to the pro coaching ranks in 2023. He spent two years as a pitching coach with High-A Cedar Rapids. Lovin was bumped to Triple-A in 2025. He had more of a roving position this past season as minor league assistant pitching coordinator.

articles.title: Mariners Notes: Infield Needs, Trade Candidates, Sloan
body: The Mariners are in the market for a boost on the left side of the infield. The flexibility of infielder Colt Emerson means the addition could be a shortstop or a third baseman, relays Adam Jude of the Seattle Times.

“We really appreciate the fact that Colt is versatile enough to go be our best third baseman on any given day,” president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said. “Our resting point right now is that we go into the season and Colt is our shortstop, but we don’t want to limit ourselves or limit our targets in an offseason acquisition to just a third baseman.”

Veteran J.P. Crawford took most of the reps at shortstop this past season, with Emerson and others filling in behind him. Both Crawford and Emerson also saw time at third base, along with trade acquisition Brendan Donovan. As a team, Seattle ranked dead last in OPS at the hot corner. Crawford is a free agent, and the club prefers to use Donovan in a more versatile role instead of installing him as the everyday option at third base.

Per Jude, Dipoto suggested that a trade was the most likely route toward finding an upgrade in the infield. The top exec mentioned that improving the infield defense on the left side was also a priority, which is part of the reason Donovan (-4 Defensive Runs Saved at 3B) is best-suited elsewhere. Emerson was a neutral defender at shortstop and a slight negative at third base.

articles.title: The Opener: MVPs, Phillips
body: Awards season is officially over. Not many surprises this year, though the players receiving down-ballot MVP votes are always intriguing.

A massive 40/40 season earned Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong the NL MVP award. It was a unanimous decision. Dodgers slugger Shohei Ohtani finished second, followed by Brewers second baseman Brice Turang. PCA was the engine of an offense that led the league in scoring. He recorded 9.8 WAR per Baseball Reference and 10.6 WAR per FanGraphs. Both marks easily paced all players. Some interesting names to receive down-ballot votes were free agent first basemen Jake Bauers and Ty France, along with the Nationals duo of James Wood and CJ Abrams.

It was also a unanimous choice on the AL side. Yordan Alvarez of the Astros received the AL MVP after a dominant offensive season. Alvarez slashed.316/.432/.601 with 42 homers and 100+ runs and RBI. He led all hitters by a massive margin with a 181 wRC+. PCA was next at 157. Rays third baseman Junior Caminero was the clear runner-up, garnering 27 of 30 second-place votes. Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. rounded out the group. Others receiving votes included Guardians closer Cade Smith and Rangers utilityman Ezequiel Duran. Full voting results can be found here.

articles.title: Braves Sign Evan Phillips To Three-Year Deal
body: The Braves have made their first significant splash of the offseason, announcing Thursday that they’ve signed right-hander Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35MM contract. The Apex Baseball client will be paid $11MM in 2027 and 2028 before earning $13MM in 2029.

Phillips, now 32 years old, returns to the organization that originally drafted him in the 17th round back in 2015. He made a brief major league debut with Atlanta in 2018, pitching 6 1/3 innings, before being traded to Baltimore alongside Bruce Zimmermann and Brett Cumberland in the deal that brought Kevin Gausman and Darren O’Day to Atlanta.

Phillips spent three years as a depth arm in the Orioles’ bullpen, shuffling between Triple-A Norfolk and Baltimore a dozen times before being released. The Rays signed Phillips to a minor league deal and gave him all of three innings before designating him for assignment. The Dodgers swooped in at that point, claiming Phillips off waivers, and the rest is history.

From 2022-25, Phillips was an absolute powerhouse in the Los Angeles bullpen. He pitched 184 2/3 regular season innings and logged a minuscule 2.14 ERA with a 29.6% strikeout rate, 6.6% walk rate and 43.3% ground-ball rate. He spent time both as a setup man and closer in that window, compiling 36 holds and 45 saves — converting on 90% of the opportunities he received along the way. Phillips sat 96.2 mph on his heater in that time. His opponents averaged an awful 86.7 mph off the bat with just a 33.5% hard-hit rate in that time. His ERA over that period ranked sixth among 253 qualified relieves.

articles.title: Latest On Jazz Chisholm’s Market
body: Jazz Chisholm Jr. is one of the bigger upside plays in the free agent position player class. He’s coming off a pedestrian.231/.312/.399 slash line but is a year removed from a 30-30 season. Chisholm is one of the top up-the-middle players available, relatively young at age 29, and hits the market unencumbered by the qualifying offer.

While the Yankees used Chisholm as a full-time second baseman in 2026, Shi Davidi of Sportsnet writes that he’s signaled a willingness to play a multi-positional role next year. Chisholm has played more than 3300 career innings at the keystone. He started 73 games at third base for the Yankees from 2024-25. The Marlins gave him 186 starts in center field between 2023-24. Chisholm also had a bit of early-career experience as a shortstop, though he hasn’t played there in five years.

The two-time All-Star said in 2025 that he felt more comfortable playing on the infield (link via Ronald Blum of The Associated Press). Davidi writes that Chisholm is willing play the outfield with his next team, though, and his plus speed should allow him to cover a decent amount of ground. Defensive metrics were split on Chisholm’s earlier outfield work. Defensive Runs Saved panned his center field play (-13 DRS), but Statcast was more favorable on both his reads and overall range (+5 Outs Above Average). Statcast has also been more bullish on Chisholm’s second base performance over the last couple seasons.

articles.title: Rangers Interested In Teruaki Sato
body: The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Teruaki Sato, report Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic. The NPB star has also been tied to the Padres, Yankees, Mets, Phillies and Diamondbacks.

Texas would be a long shot given his expected price tag. The Rangers have seemingly been more focused on shedding some of their significant obligations to any of Corey Seager, Jacob deGrom or Nathan Eovaldi. Sato is arguably the top position player in this year’s free agent class. MLBTR predicted a five-year, $80MM deal; other public estimates on his market value have been in the nine-figure range. His signing team would also need to pay a posting fee proportional to the contract value. Players making the move from foreign leagues have a wider range of outcomes, so perhaps the Rangers are monitoring in case Sato’s market collapses similarly to Munetaka Murakami’s a year ago.

There’s obviously no harm for Texas in doing their diligence from a scouting perspective. Sato, who’s entering his age-28 season, is a left-handed hitter with huge power. He hit 39 home runs for the Hashin Tigers this year, one season after connecting on 40. Sato is coming off a.306/.383/.609 slash line across 614 plate appearances.

articles.title: Kurt Suzuki Remaining With Angels As Special Assistant
body: Kurt Suzuki will remain in the Angels organization as a special assistant in the front office, interim general manager John Mozeliak told reporters at the GM Meetings earlier this week (link via Jeff Fletcher of The Orange County Register). The Halos declined their option on Suzuki after one season in the managerial role.

The former All-Star catcher had a difficult assignment in his lone managerial season. He signed a one-year contract, an atypically short commitment for any manager. Suzuki took over one of the worst rosters in MLB coming off a 72-90 season. They lost 100 games for the first time in club history this year. The Angels fired GM Perry Minasian in June and are in the middle of a sale process at the ownership level.

It clearly wasn’t an ideal situation for a first-time skipper. The Angels unsurprisingly went in a different direction. Stan Kroenke’s group is still awaiting official approval on the ownership transfer. They’ll hire a permanent GM at that point, as Mozeliak is expected to step aside when his contract expires next month. The new front office can then make a managerial hire, which might not happen until midway through the lockout.

Suzuki spent the 2023-25 seasons in the same special assistant role to which he now returns. It wouldn’t be a surprise if he pursues coaching or managerial opportunities in future years. Suzuki is highly respected around the league and interviewed for the Giants’ managerial vacancy last fall.

articles.title: Multiple Teams Interested In Dustin May
body: 7:35pm: Barry Jackson of The Miami Herald reports that the Marlins have also given some consideration to a May pursuit.

9:50am: Former Brewers right-hander Dustin May is receiving widespread interest as a free agent, reports Jon Morosi of MLB Network. Morosi links the Astros, Cubs, Padres, and White Sox to the veteran righty.

It’s the second straight winter on the open market for May. Last time around, he landed a one-year, $12.5MM contract with the Cardinals. May was coming off an uneven season split between the Dodgers and Red Sox. He came over in the deadline deal that sent outfield prospects James Tibbs III and Zach Ehrhard to Los Angeles.

St. Louis grabbed May to cover innings in a rotation lacking proven options. It ended up being a surprisingly steady group. Michael McGreevy, Andre Pallante, Kyle Leahy, and Matthew Liberatore each made 29+ starts and tossed 140+ innings. May was right there with them, though his final 10 outings came in Milwaukee. Quinn Mathews filled May’s role after the trade.

May wound up on the future World Series champs as part of a trade deadline move that sent him to the Brewers with reliever JoJo Romero for outfield prospects Alexander Frias and Josiah Ragsdale. The May trade tree could end up being pretty interesting given the ceilings of Tibbs and Frias. May wasn’t particularly effective in Milwaukee, posting a 5.65 ERA over 36 2/3 innings to close the regular season. He allowed seven earned runs in 11 postseason frames.

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Wins NL MVP Award
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced Thursday that Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong has been named the National League’s Most Valuable Player. Shohei Ohtani and Brice Turang placed second and third, respectively. Crow-Armstrong received all 30 first-place votes, giving us unanimous winners in both leagues.

Crow-Armstrong snaps Ohtani’s streak of three consecutive MVP wins behind a massive season on both sides of the ball. The 24-year-old outfielder was easily the best player in baseball this year. He tied Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead with 45 home runs, adding 31 doubles and eight triples. His 84 extra-base hits easily led the NL, nine clear of Matt Olson in second place. He added 41 steals in 48 attempts, making him the only player in the majors this year to go 40-40. It’s one of seven such seasons in baseball history.

The accolades don’t stop there. Crow-Armstrong led qualified National League hitters with a.570 slugging percentage and.943 OPS. He batted.280/.372/.570 across an NL-leading 726 plate appearances. He led the majors with 119 runs scored and was third in the NL with 107 RBI. He and Turang were the only NL hitters to both score and drive in 100 runs.

articles.title: Padres Have Received Interest In Freddy Fermin, Luis Campusano
body: The Padres have gotten calls from other teams on catchers Freddy Fermin and Luis Campusano, writes Kevin Acee of The San Diego Union-Tribune. Acee reports that San Diego is likely to trade one of those players this offseason.

Catching should be an organizational strength for years. Ethan Salas, who has a case as the #1 prospect in baseball, made a late-season debut at age 20. Salas will hopefully be the franchise catcher. There’s a good chance he’ll break camp, as San Diego trusted him enough to start him for three games in the postseason. Scouting reports rave about Salas’ defensive tools and advanced leadership and game-calling skills. He’s also coming off a.296/.374/.448 showing against older pitching between the top two minor league levels.

Salas’ emergence naturally makes one of the experienced catchers more expendable. Fermin is a superlative defender who hit.203/.274/.315 in 96 games this year. The bat is probably too light for him to be a #1 catcher on a contender, but he excels in all aspects behind the plate. He’s an above-average pitch framer, an elite blocker, and one of the best catch-and-throw backstops in the league. Fermin has also built a strong reputation as a leader of pitching staffs in Kansas City and San Diego.

articles.title: Yordan Alvarez Wins AL MVP Award
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced Thursday that Yordan Alvarez has been named the Most Valuable Player in the American League. Alvarez won the award unanimously, collecting all 30 first-place votes. Junior Caminero and Bobby Witt Jr. finished second and third, respectively.

Alvarez has been an elite hitter for the entirety of his career. He took his game to another level at age 29, topping 40 home runs for the first time. Alvarez was the best offensive player in the sport this year, leading qualified hitters in all three slash stats (as well as OPS, of course). He batted.316/.432/.601 with 42 longballs in a career-high 692 plate appearances. Alvarez walked almost as often as he struck out while remaining arguably the premier power threat in the American League.

Caminero and Alvarez tied for second in the AL and fourth in the majors with the 42 longballs. (Pete Alonso seized the AL home run crown with a two-homer game in the final weekend of the season, finishing the year at 43.) Alvarez scored 105 runs and drove in 106, a top three mark among AL hitters in both categories. He fairly comfortably beat out Chandler Simpson (.306) to win his first batting title and maintained a five-point edge on NL leader Gabriel Moreno in that regard.

articles.title: Mets, Yankees Met With Alec Bohm At GM Meetings
body: Free agent infielder Alec Bohm met with both the Yankees and Mets at this week’s general managers’ meetings in Las Vegas, according to reporting from Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic. The connection to the Yankees was previously reported.

Rosenthal and Sammon specify that the Mets would be interested in Bohm at first base, which makes a lot of sense. For one thing, the Mets already have a third baseman in Bo Bichette, whereas first base is more open.

Bohm has played both corner spots but his glovework at third has never been highly regarded. In almost 6,000 career innings at third base, he has a grade of minus-58 from Defensive Runs Saved. From 2020 to the present, that’s the worst DRS mark of any third baseman and tied for second-worst of any player at any position. Jose Altuve’s minus-73 mark at second base is the only person beyond Bohm in that regard. Bohm’s minus-15 grade from Outs Above Average and minus-16 from Fielding Run Value aren’t quite as extreme but still subpar.

Due to his poor work at third, he has spent more time at first as his career has gone on. His defensive grades at first are also subpar but aren’t as bad, especially when focusing on more recent seasons. Bohm has a grade of minus-4 DRS at first in his career but was above average in both 2025 and 2026. He has minus-8 OAA and minus-7 FRV for his career but has been close to par over the past three campaigns.

articles.title: Giants Hire James Rowson As Offensive Coordinator
body: 5:05pm: The Giants have now officially announced Rowson’s hiring.

2:26pm: The Giants are expected to hire former Yankees hitting coach James Rowson to the big-league staff, as first reported by Robert Murray of FanSided. Rowson’s title will be offensive coordinator, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post.

It hadn’t been clear that Rowson was departing New York, but general manager Brian Cashman referred to him as a “free agent” this week. He lands in San Francisco after three seasons with the Yankees. The Giants lost hitting coach Hunter Mense this offseason. Mense took a gig with the Royals.

After a brief minor league career, Rowson got into coaching. He started in the Angels organization as a minor league hitting coach in 2002. He spent six years in the Yankees’ system in the same position. Rowson earned his first look in the majors with the Cubs midway through the 2012 season. He took over for Rudy Jaramillo, who was fired after a slow offensive start. Rowson ditched the interim tag and stayed aboard the following season.

Rowson had stops with the Twins, Marlins, and Tigers in various roles before joining manager Aaron Boone’s staff in 2024. The Yankees have been a strong offense in Rowson’s three years with the club. New York has ranked top 10 in scoring in each season, including a league-leading 849 runs in 2025.

articles.title: Brewers To Have Fourth Option On Jeferson Quero
body: The Brewers will have a fourth option year for catcher Jeferson Quero in 2027, reports Matt Trueblood of Brewer Fanatic. That’s a notable development for the Brewers, as it will be easier to keep Quero on the roster next year.

Normally, a player has three option years. If a player on the 40-man roster is optionable, a team can send him to the minors without exposing him to waivers. If the player spends at least 20 days of a season on optional assignment, he uses up one of those options.

Quero was added to Milwaukee’s 40-man roster in November of 2023 to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft. He has mostly been in the minors since then. His major league track record consists of just one game in March of this year. He therefore burned his three option seasons in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

A team can be granted a fourth option on a player if he has exhausted the first three and hasn’t yet played five full seasons. A “full” season is one in which the player is active for at least 90 days, majors and minors combined, or one in which the player was active for 30 days and his active/injured list time added up to at least 90 days. Basically, these parameters are to exclude short-season rookie ball campaigns as “full” seasons, or situations where a player misses an entire year due to a significant injury.

articles.title: Yankees Notes: Infield, Catcher, Bullpen
body: The Yankees have been busy checking in on various offseason pursuits, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post, but might also slow-play the market. Heyman says the Yankees have talked to the Rangers about Corey Seager and checked in with free agents Luis Arraez, Brandon Lowe and Carson Kelly. But broadly, Heyman frames it as possible that the Yankees play things cool in the pre-lockout period.

Heyman points out that owner Hal Steinbrenner is a big proponent of a salary cap, which isn’t surprising. Unlike his father, who was always happy to use financial might to push the Yankees ahead, the younger Steinbrenner has often expressed unease with that approach. A couple of years ago, he described the Yankees’ spending as “unsustainable.”

Per the MLBTR Payroll Tracker, the Yankees had a competitive balance tax number of $342MM in 2026. They are projected for $282MM next year, before even making any significant moves. In the ongoing collective bargaining talks, MLB has proposed a cap of $258.2MM. That would start in 2028, though it’s a loose figure, as 2027 league revenues could move the line.

It’s unlikely that a cap will actually be in place, at 2028 or any other time. The MLB Players Association is opposed to a cap and has no intention of agreeing to one. Even if they are eventually persuaded, the actual number would surely change in future proposals.

articles.title: Rangers To Hire Tommy Joseph As Assistant Hitting Coach
body: The Rangers are expected to add Tommy Joseph to the coaching staff, per Shawn McFarland of the Dallas Morning News. Joseph will serve as an assistant under lead hitting coach Justin Viele.

Joseph has bounced around frequently since joining the coaching ranks in 2021. He got his start as a minor league hitting coach in the Mets system. He took a similar position in 2023 with the Giants. Joseph joined a big-league staff for the first time in 2024, operating as an assistant hitting coach for the Mariners. He most recently worked in the same position with the Orioles.

McFarland adds that Eric Dorton will be retained as an assistant hitting coach. Viele and Dorton joined the organization last season under new manager Skip Schumaker. President of baseball operations Chris Young praised Viele for his efforts in 2026.

“I think he’s done very good things,” Young said, relayed by McFarland. “It didn’t perfectly translate to the run production we needed last year, but, there were improvements offensively in the overall performance. Now we’ve got to translate that individually to the collective and our ability to score runs as a collective group.”

articles.title: Brandon Marsh Underwent Hand Surgery At End Of Season
body: Phillies outfielder Brandon Marsh underwent surgery on his left hand, just above the wrist, reports Matt Gelb of The Athletic. The procedure took place just after the season ended. There was no public information about a hand injury for Marsh during the season but Gelb says he played through it for months. It’s unclear if team personnel knew about the issue. Gelb adds that Marsh is available in trade talks this offseason as the Phillies are telling other clubs they aren’t locked into anything in the outfield.

It’s possible that the injury explains Marsh’s uneven 2026 season, as he had a great first half and an awful second half. Marsh had a.301/.339/.490 batting line through the All-Star break. That was propped up a bit by a.377 batting average on balls in play but Marsh also hit 15 home runs. After the break, Marsh hit just.184/.243/.259. Part of that was his BABIP swinging the other way to.225 but he also only hit three home runs.

There is some data to suggest Marsh wasn’t impacting the ball as much as the season went on. He had a 50% hard hit rate in April and was in the mid-40s in May and June. He was at 40% in July and August and then was down to 31.7% in September. His average exit velocity had a similar slide, going from 91.4 miles per hour in April to 86.3 mph by the final month of the season. Marsh ended up with a.260/.304/.408 line and 90 wRC+ at season’s end. Over the prior three seasons, he hit.268/.347/.440 for a 115 wRC+, so this year’s production was clearly down on the whole.

articles.title: Dodgers Notes: Hernandez, Vesia, Phillips, Infielders
body: With a thin market for righty-swinging outfielders this winter, the Dodgers are once again expected to receive trade interest in Teoscar Hernandez. The veteran is heading into the final season of his three-year contract with Los Angeles.

General manager Brandon Gomes downplayed moving anyone on the big-league club at the GM Meetings this week. “We feel really good about our team as is and certainly don’t feel compelled to do anything along those lines,” Gomes told reporters, including Jack Harris of the California Post.

Hernandez is set to make $14.5MM this season. The Dodgers hold a $15MM club option on him for 2028, with a $6.5MM buyout. Assuming his option isn’t picked up, it amounts to a $21MM price tag for a season of Hernandez, who delivered another above-average year at the plate in 2026.

Hernandez, now 34, got off to a solid start this year. He carried a.785 OPS near the end of May before going down with a hamstring injury. The veteran scuffled to a.220/.273/.353 line through August after a month-long stint on the IL. He picked it back up with a.965 OPS in September, but struggled in the postseason. The end result was a 110 wRC+ with 16 homers across 491 plate appearances.

The emergence of top prospect Josue De Paula would make it easier to part ways with Hernandez, at least at the plate. De Paula piled up 10 hits and 11 walks in a brief 11-game stint to close the regular season. He got on base at an absurd.500 clip. It’s a small sample, but De Paula appears ready to contribute in the majors.

articles.title: Braves, Tyler Freeman Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Braves and utilityman Tyler Freeman are in agreement on a minor league contract, reports Thomas Harding of MLB.com. The Paragon Sports International client will be in big league camp as a non-roster invitee ahead of the 2027 season. Harding adds that Freeman had back surgery in October but believes he’ll be ready for game action by late March.

Freeman, 27, was the No. 71 overall pick by Cleveland back in 2017. He ranked as one of their top prospects for several years and garnered top-100 fanfare from 2020-22. He’s yet to deliver on that prospect billing to date, however. In parts of five big league seasons, the righty-swinging infielder/outfielder carries a.247/.323/.336 batting line. He’s walked at a middling 6.4% clip but also shown the excellent contact skills that helped make him such a well-regarded prospect, fanning in only 13.4% of his plate appearances.

Scouting reports on Freeman have never really settled on where he fits best defensively. His plus-plus hit tool and above-average speed give him the potential to be a genuine contributor, but he’s struggled defensively at second base, third base, shortstop and across all three outfield positions. Freeman drew poor marks for his throwing in the infield earlier in his career. His arm has graded out with borderline elite strength since moving to more of an outfield role, but he’s not especially accurate with it and struggles with his reads/jumps on the grass.

articles.title: Nationals Unlikely To Trade CJ Abrams
body: As the Nationals’ rebuild has lasted longer than anticipated — leading to a front office overhaul — CJ Abrams’ name has frequented the rumor circuit over the past few years as a result. However, Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic reports that multiple executives from around the league have suggested at this week’s GM Meetings that the Nats seem less inclined to seriously entertain offers on their star infielder (video link). The Nationals are currently planning to hang onto Abrams for the upcoming season.

As with any trade scenario, things can change in a heartbeat. It’s not likely to happen, but if a team called and offered Washington one of the game’s two or three best prospects to get the ball rolling, Nats president of baseball ops Paul Toboni would surely at least have a conversation. That’s a pure hypothetical, to be clear, but that sort of unexpected push from a rival front office can always make a team change its tune on an in-house player it plans to keep.

Abrams is entering his sixth big league season despite the fact that he only turned 26 after the season ended. The former No. 6 overall draft pick (Padres, 2019) was one of the sport’s top prospects and one of the headline pieces who went from San Diego to Washington in 2022’s Juan Soto blockbuster. Abrams, James Wood, MacKenzie Gore, Robert Hassell III and current top prospect Jarlin Susana were all traded from the Padres to the Nats, who were selling off two-plus seasons of control over Soto after he rejected a reported extension offer north of $400MM.

articles.title: Mets To Hire Derek Johnson
body: The Mets are expected to hire former pitching coach Derek Johnson, as first reported by Bobby Nightengale of the Minnesota Star Tribune. Will Sammon of The Athletic adds that Johnson will serve in an advisory role with New York.

Johnson has been a big-league pitching coach for the past decade. After three seasons as a minor league pitching coordinator with the Cubs, he became the Brewers pitching coach in 2016. Johnson remained in the NL Central for his next gig, joining the Reds as pitching coach in 2019. Cincinnati extended Johnson and named him the director of pitching after the 2021 campaign.

The Reds officially parted ways with Johnson at the end of the season, though he hadn’t been with the club for several months. Johnson stepped away for personal reasons in June. President of baseball operations Nick Krall announced in October that Johnson wouldn’t be returning to the team.

Cincinnati has developed a solid group of starters in recent years. Hunter Greene cleaned up his command and has been an ace-caliber arm when healthy. Chase Burns delivered a stellar first full season in the majors this past year. Both Greene and Burns are former first-rounders with elite stuff, but the team has also been able to get strong results out of Andrew Abbott. A flyball pitcher in Great American Ball Park seems like a tricky proposition, though Abbott has made it work.

articles.title: Blue Jays Notes: Infield, Outfield, Rotation, Bullpen, Barger
body: It’s common for the Blue Jays to explore all avenues in the offseason and it doesn’t seem as though this winter will be any different. Reporting from the general managers’ meetings in Las Vegas, Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet (two columns) and Mitch Bannon of The Athletic (two columns) have details on their pursuits in the infield, the outfield, the rotation and the bullpen.

It is known that the Jays are looking to shake-up the middle infield. The 2026 club had Andrés Giménez at shortstop and Ernie Clement at second base. Clement’s performance declined this year relative to 2025, both offensively and defensively. There’s an argument for the Jays to get a middle infielder, therefore pushing Giménez and Clement together into a platoon, either at shortstop or second base. Clement could also bounce around to other positions in a utility capacity.

The Jays reportedly looked into middle infield options at the deadline, though they didn’t pull the trigger there. After the season, general manager Ross Atkins admitted that Clement would probably have to earn a regular role in 2027.

articles.title: Red Sox Rumors: Suzuki, Jeffers, Duran, Breslow
body: The Red Sox have reached out to free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki and have interest in free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers, per reports from Pete Abraham of the Boston Globe and Jon Heyman of the New York Post, respectively. Either slugger would add some right-handed thump to a Boston lineup that is lacking in right-handed power options. They’re both imperfect fits, given the current composition of the roster, but interest in both signals a desire to balance out a lefty-heavy lineup.

Suzuki could slot into an outfield corner and also take some DH at-bats. The Sox have Ceddanne Rafaela locked into center field with Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida as lefty-swinging corner outfield/DH options. That doesn’t leave much room for Suzuki, but Abraham fittingly adds that Boston is actively shopping Duran in what has been one of the “worst kept secrets” of this week’s GM Meetings. Yoshida, meanwhile, is entering the final year of his contract. The Sox didn’t find a trade partner last offseason, but with one year to go, he could be easier to move and could even be a release candidate.

articles.title: Guardians Planning To Raise Payroll, Exploring Rotation Market
body: The Guardians are planning to increase payroll for the 2027 season and have been exploring the market to add starting pitching, reports Zack Meisel of The Athletic. Jon Heyman of the New York Post, meanwhile, reports that Cleveland has some interest in left-handed reliever Tim Hill, who’s spent the past two and a half seasons with the Yankees but reached the open market at season’s end.

A payroll increase is a welcome development for Guards fans, though there’s really nowhere to go but up. Cleveland opened the 2026 season with a payroll around $75MM, and that’s before factoring in José Ramírez’s $10MM in deferred salary or the $6MM salary that closer Emmanuel Clase didn’t collect while spending time on the restricted list during the ongoing federal probe into his gambling/pitch-rigging scandal.

President of baseball operations Chris Antonetti didn’t provide a specific number to Meisel but did explicitly state payroll would increase. Much of that will be natural. Tanner Bibee’s five-year contract calls for his salary to jump from $4MM to $7MM.

articles.title: Giants In Closing Market, Unlikely To Sign Qualified Free Agent
body: Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey provided some updates on the team’s offseason plans in talks with reporters at the GM Meetings this week. Andrew Baggarly of The Athletic and Shayna Rubin of The San Francisco Chronicle were among those to relay his quotes.

For the second straight offseason, Posey downplayed the idea that the Giants would play at the top of the free agent market. He suggested they were unlikely to surrender any draft capital by signing one of the eight players who rejected a qualifying offer, saying those moves would “be harder for us.” That alone wouldn’t rule them out on Tarik Skubal, Michael King or Freddy Peralta — none of whom were eligible for the QO. Trevor Rogers is the only starting pitcher who received a qualifying offer.

Rubin reports that the Giants have touched base with Peralta but appear focused on pitchers who’ll sign shorter-term contracts. Skubal prefers a long-term arrangement and would surely only go short term for a monster average annual value. Peralta seemed like a candidate for a pillow contract when he was struggling with the Mets, but his late-season turnaround in Tampa Bay might’ve been enough to put a five-plus year deal back on the table. King is entering his age-32 season and unlikely to exceed four years but could command $20-25MM on an annual basis.

articles.title: Louis Varland, Mason Miller Named BBWAA Relievers Of The Year
body: In addition to tonight’s Cy Young announcements, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced the results of their inaugural Reliever of the Year voting. Toronto’s Louis Varland and San Diego’s Mason Miller are the first honorees in the respective leagues.

Varland got the edge over Cleveland’s Cade Smith and Tampa Bay’s Bryan Baker in the American League. Acquired from Minnesota at the 2025 deadline, Varland opened the season in a setup role. Jeff Hoffman’s early struggles opened the ninth inning at the end of April. Varland took the job and never looked back, going 35-37 in save chances. He fired 78 innings with a sterling 1.27 earned run average while striking out a career-high 31.6% of opposing hitters.

The 28-year-old Varland tied Aroldis Chapman and David Bednar for third in the AL in saves, trailing the aforementioned Smith and Baker (41 apiece). He had the lowest ERA among AL relievers with 50+ innings pitched, ranked sixth in strikeout rate, and fifth in overall strikeouts.

It was a tightly contested race. Baker and Smith not only had gaudier save totals, they were similarly dominant on a batter for batter basis. All three finalists had a sub-2.00 earned run average. Smith’s 36.3% strikeout rate was second-best in the American League (behind Andrés Muñoz), while his 1.95 ERA ranked eighth. Baker was second in ERA at 1.44 but outside the top 25 with a strong but not overwhelming 25.8% strikeout percentage.

articles.title: Latest On Randy Arozarena’s Market
body: Randy Arozarena is one of the top bats available in a weak free agent hitting market. The incumbent Mariners issued a qualifying offer but are expected to move on, content to receive the compensatory pick after the first round when he inevitably signs for at least $50MM with another club. The Seattle Times has reported that the Cuban-born Arozarena may prefer to move back to the East Coast, where he spent four and a half seasons in Tampa Bay before the 2024 deadline trade to Seattle.

The Phillies have reportedly shown some interest as they scour the top of the outfield market. At the same time, Philadelphia president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski expressed some trepidation about adding another big contract to one of the older rosters in the league. Arozarena is entering his age-32 season and will cost a signing club draft compensation once he officially declines the QO. Philadelphia, as luxury tax payors, would be subject to the highest penalties: their second- and fifth-highest picks in 2027, plus $1MM from their international amateur bonus pool.

articles.title: Latest On Yankees, Alec Bohm
body: 8:40pm: Brendan Kuty of The Athletic writes that a source suggested the Yankees have not shown much interest in Bohm to this point. Kuty leaves open the possibility that the club could show interest in the offseason.

1:00pm: The Yankees have had a tough time finding a steady third baseman for multiple years. Addressing the hot corner will likely be a priority this offseason, and the club has been connected to one of the bigger names on the market. New York has interest in Alec Bohm, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post.

Bohm has spent his entire pro career with the Phillies. After several years as an above-average bat, he struggled on the verge of free agency. Bohm finished with a 90 wRC+ across 629 plate appearances. He hit 15 homers and drove in 88 runs.

It’s not an ideal offseason to be hunting for a third baseman. Bohm is arguably the only everyday regular available, unless you include utilityman Mauricio Dubon. NPB import Teruaki Sato is also a fringy inclusion given the uncertainty around his ability to handle the position as a big leaguer. The list also includes uninspiring veterans like Yoan Moncada, Luis Rengifo, Edmundo Sosa, and Ramon Urias.

After the failed Jazz Chisholm Jr. experiment, the Yankees went out and acquired Ryan McMahon to take over at third base midway through 2025. The former Rockie underwhelmed at the plate, but delivered 7 Defensive Runs Saved. McMahon was a well-below-league-average bat once again in 2026. More notably, he posted -3 DRS at third base.

articles.title: Mariners Notes: Donovan, Happ, Rotation
body: 8:19pm: Jude downplays the Happ connection, reporting that both he and NPB star Teruaki Sato are unlikely fits for the Mariners.

5:49pm: The Mariners are looking for offensive help and the versatility of Brendan Donovan could be an important factor in that search. Adam Jude and Ryan Divish of The Seattle Times report that the M’s are looking for two bats, with a preference for righties. Ideally, one of these bats would play on the left side of the infield. That could push Donovan from the infield to left field next year with the expected departure of Randy Arozarena.

Donovan’s first year in Seattle was a bust. He went on the injured list multiple times due to groin issues and a concussion. He only got into 39 games on the year. He continued to perform when healthy enough to take the field. He hit.277/.371/.409 in his 159 plate appearances, fairly similar to his career line of.282/.362/.411. Defensively, Donovan has experience everywhere except for center field and the battery.

The M’s could keep him at third base next year, next to shortstop Colt Emerson. However, the report from Jude and Divish notes that the Mariners are hoping to improve their infield defense. Defensive metrics like Donovan’s work at third base in his career but he fared poorly in 2026. He was ranked as below average by each of Defensive Runs Saved, Outs Above Average and Fielding Run Value. Emerson also didn’t grade out well in his rookie season at shortstop or third, so it seems the Mariners are open to shaking things up.

articles.title: Ryan Jeffers To Decline Qualifying Offer
body: Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers is declining the qualifying offer, reports Bobby Nightengale of The Minnesota Star-Tribune. Minnesota’s front office certainly expected as much, and they have ongoing interest in bringing Jeffers back on a multi-year deal.

MLBTR predicted Jeffers to receive a four-year, $75MM contract in ranking him ninth on our Top 50 Free Agents list. That came with the assumption that Jeffers would reject the QO, as he’s the clear #1 option in the catching class. The righty hitter is coming off a.256/.353/.461 slash with 14 homers and career-best strikeout and walk numbers. Although he was limited to 368 plate appearances by a hamate fracture, Jeffers has a four-year track record of strong offense behind the dish (.254/.342/.440 in more than 1600 plate appearances).

Jeffers is entering his age-30 season. He’s a passable but hardly elite defender who could end up at first base toward the end of a three- or four-year contract. Jeffers has the bat to profile there and has a particularly strong career track record versus left-handed pitching. He’s fairly similar statistically to Willson Contreras when he commanded a five-year, $87.5MM deal from St. Louis. Jeffers doesn’t have the same pedigree — Contreras was a three-time All-Star who’d been the primary catcher on a World Series team — but should do well on the open market.

articles.title: Jacob Misiorowski Wins NL Cy Young Award
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced Wednesday that Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski won the NL Cy Young award. Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez and Atlanta’s Chris Sale finished second and third, respectively.

Misiorowski, like his AL counterpart Cam Schlittler, won the award unanimously. There wasn’t much intrigue beyond that in either league, as it’s been clear for months who’d take home the hardware. Misiorowski had the lowest earned run average (1.80) of any qualified pitcher in baseball. He threw 174 2/3 innings across 30 starts, overpowering hitters with unprecedented velocity and huge extension on his 6’7″ frame.

Milwaukee’s star righty struck out 37.9% of opposing hitters, three points higher than any other qualifier in either league. Even including relievers, only Mason Miller was tougher to hit on a batter for batter basis. Misiorowski only walked 6.6% of opponents, firmly putting to rest any questions he faced as a prospect about whether his control might push him to the bullpen. He led the majors with 252 strikeouts despite tying for 22nd in innings.

Opposing hitters managed a putrid.157/.224/.246 slash line against Misiorowski across 665 plate appearances. He went 16-5 and the Brew Crew were 22-8 overall in his starts. While it’s irrelevant to awards consideration, they also won all four times he took the ball in the playoffs. Misiorowski tossed 19 frames of four-run ball in October, capping the season with 5 2/3 scoreless in the Game 5 clincher in the World Series.

articles.title: Cam Schlittler Wins AL Cy Young Award
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced that Cam Schlittler has won the AL Cy Young award. The Yankees ace appeared at the top on all 30 ballots. Toronto’s Dylan Cease is runner-up, while Cleveland rookie Parker Messick finished in third place.

To the extent there was any suspense about this result, it was only whether Schlittler’s win would be unanimous. The 6’6″ righty had a dominant first full season in the big leagues. Schlittler made 33 starts and fired 193 2/3 innings of 1.95 ERA ball. He was the only qualified pitcher in the AL with a sub-2.00 mark. Schlittler was second in the league behind Michael Wacha in innings and third — behind Gavin Williams and Cease — with 239 strikeouts. Only Williams had a higher difference between his strikeout and walk rates.

Schlittler finished with a 14-6 record; the Yankees went 21-12 in his starts overall. He led AL pitchers in Wins Above Replacement at both FanGraphs (6.2) and Baseball Reference (7.0). It’s a convincing case in terms of both traditional and advanced metrics that left little doubt that Schlittler would earn his first Cy Young honors. He also earned his first All-Star selection over the summer.

articles.title: Mets Eyeing Left-Handed Relievers
body: 6:07pm: Another former Met is also on the radar in the lefty relief search. Jon Heyman of The New York Post reports that they’ve checked in on A.J. Minter, who’s back on the market after they traded him to Minnesota at the deadline. Minter combined for a 2.56 ERA with a 22% strikeout rate across 45 2/3 innings this year.

1:42pm: The Mets, like just about every club in the game, are looking to strengthen their bullpen this winter. They’ll pursue a wide variety of options, but lefties Alex Vesia and Tim Hill are among their early targets, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. Vesia’s market is particularly competitive, Sammon notes, with around half the league expressing genuine interest to this point.

Joel Sherman of the New York Post adds that the Mets have also spoken with the reps for lefty Darwinzon Hernández, who’s eyeing a major league comeback after a strong three-year run in Japan. SNY’s Chelsea Janes, meanwhile, notes that the Mets have talked to Brooks Raley about a potential reunion.

articles.title: Phillies Interested In Teruaki Sato, Seiya Suzuki, Randy Arozarena
body: The Phillies are in the market for the top outfield free agents. Matt Gelb of The Athletic reports that the Phils have interest in Teruaki Sato, Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki. Sato has mostly been a third baseman in his career in Japan but he has some right field experience and Gelb specifies the Phillies would be looking at him as a corner outfielder.

It’s not a surprise that the Phillies are looking for outfield help, as they have plenty of uncertainty on the grass. They started the 2026 season with Brandon Marsh, Justin Crawford and Adolis García as their regulars out there. García played poorly for 67 games and then required season-ending shoulder surgery. He is now a free agent. Crawford stole 17 bases but hit just.264/.309/.353 with poor defensive metrics to boot. Marsh hit 18 home runs but his 6% walk rate was subpar, leading to a.260/.304/.408 line and 90 wRC+. He finished on a down note, as he hit.301/.339/.490 in the first half and.184/.243/.259 in the second.

After the deadline, the Phillies shook thing up. They acquired Luis Arraez and put him at second base. That moved Bryson Stott to third base, bumping Alec Bohm to first base and Bryce Harper to right field. Harper’s glovework in right was graded poorly. With Arraez and Bohm now free agents, he projects to return to first base next year.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Notes: Sato, Rotation, Marte
body: The Diamondbacks are known to be reducing payroll from 2026’s franchise-record levels as they head into the 2027 season, but they’re still keeping tabs on some big names. Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon and Katie Woo of The Athletic report that Arizona has done its due diligence on Nippon Professional Baseball star Teruaki Sato, who is available to MLB clubs after being posted by NPB’s Hanshin Tigers.

Sato, 27, is the reigning Triple Crown winner in NPB. He belted 39 home runs this past season (and hit 40 in 2025) while slashing.303/.386/.609 in 614 plate appearances. It’s the most productive season of Sato’s career. He’s steadily improved throughout his 20s in NPB, debuting with a slightly better-than-average line as a 22-year-old rookie back in 2021 but emerging as one of Japan’s best offensive players over the past two seasons.

The D-backs have a known preference for left-handed bats. Sato has been a third baseman in Japan, though he’s dabbled in the outfield corners as well. Third base is spoken for by Nolan Arenado in Arizona — but there’s been talk of Arenado potentially playing some first base. Some scouts around the league feel Sato is athletic enough to shift to the outfield and become a better defender there than he is at the hot corner, however. Arizona has some uncertainty in the outfield, where inexperienced former top prospects Jordan Lawlar and Ryan Waldschmidt are set to take regular reps in conjunction with veterans Corbin Carroll and Lars Nootbaar.

articles.title: Chris Martin Retires
body: Veteran right-hander Chris Martin has retired as a player, per Robert Murray of FanSided. He pitched in 11 different MLB seasons for seven different clubs and also spent a couple of years in Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball.

It’s not a shock that Martin is hanging up his spikes. Back in September of 2024, he said that he was 95% sure that 2025 would be his last season. In the end, the 5% won out, as Martin returned to the Rangers for the 2026 campaign. But he made multiple trips to the injured list this year due to a shoulder impingement and had poor results in the 16 games he did play. He was released in August.

Martin was born and played high school ball in Texas. The Tigers drafted him out of high school in 2004 but he didn’t sign and went to McLennan Community College. The Rockies drafted him in 2005 and went the draft-and-follow route, when that type of strategy was still allowed. Martin then required surgery on a torn labrum in shoulder. The Rockies opted not to sign him. He went undrafted in 2006 and then started his professional career in independent ball.

Due to continued shoulder troubles in indy ball, Martin thought his career was over. He took odd jobs for places like UPS, Lowe’s and an appliance warehouse. A game of catch behind that warehouse led to Martin discovering that his shoulder felt better, so he tried baseball again. After some time in indy ball, he was able to get a minor league deal with the Red Sox in 2011.

articles.title: Tigers To Sign Emilio Pagán
body: November 11: Pagán’s deal is for $11.5MM plus a bonus clause, reports Gordon Wittenmyer of the Cincinnati Enquirer.

November 10: The Tigers are in agreement with free agent reliever Emilio Pagán, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. It’s reportedly a one-year deal in the $11MM range for the Ballengee Group client. Detroit has a full 40-man roster and will need to make a corresponding move once the signing is official.

It’s this year’s first significant move on the free agent market. Pagán’s market moved quickly, as he finds a new landing spot within two weeks of declining a $10MM player option with Cincinnati. Pagán banks an extra million dollars and presumably will enter the season as A.J. Hinch’s primary closer.

The agreement comes together within hours of Detroit president of baseball operations Scott Harris telling reporters he was seeking a right-handed leverage reliever who could improve the team’s strikeout ability (links via Cody Stavenhagen of The Athletic and Jason Beck of MLB.com). Pagán fanned 25.9% of opponents this year and has a 28% strikeout rate for his career, which will make him one of the team’s better swing-and-miss arms.

Detroit’s bullpen was 19th in strikeout rate and 21st in whiffs this past season. They were near the bottom of the league in that regard in 2025 as well. It caught up to them this year, as the Tigers led the American League with 31 blown saves despite finishing middle of the pack in earned run average. Their high-leverage arms too frequently stumbled.

articles.title: Dodgers Reportedly Prefer Short-Term Deal In Skubal Bidding
body: The Dodgers are in the mix for free agent Tarik Skubal but the framework of his eventual deal could be very important. Katie Woo of The Athletic reports that their interest would be contingent on Skubal being open to a short-term deal. Jeff Passan of ESPN reports that Skubal has no interest in that kind of arrangement, which would seemingly work against the Dodgers in the bidding.

It’s not really a surprise to hear that the Dodgers are leaning this way. Though they have acquired a number of talented players over the years, they have a clear preference to avoid really long free agent deals. In the past decade, they have only twice gone longer than six years for a free agent, both under special circumstances. One was for Shohei Ohtani, the other for Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Ohtani is a unicorn talent who got a ten-year deal with the Dodgers, with almost all of the money deferred. Yamamoto got a 12-year deal because he was unusually young, coming over from Japan ahead of his age-25 season.

Though it might feel like the Dodgers always sign the top players, they are often happy to let them go elsewhere when the bidding is strong. Juan Soto got 15 years from the Mets. Bryce Harper got 13 years from the Phillies and Trea Turner 11 from that same club. Gerrit Cole and Max Fried got their deals from the Yankees and Dylan Cease ended up with the Blue Jays.

In some of those cases, the Dodgers were involved but would only pounce if the player didn’t find a satisfactory long-term deal and became open to short-term offers. This approach has been described as “hanging around the backboard.”

articles.title: Phillies, Bryan Ramos Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Phillies and free agent infielder Bryan Ramos have agreed to a minor league contract, reports Francys Romero of BeisbolFR.com. The ISE Baseball client will be in camp as a non-roster invitee ahead of the 2027 season.

Ramos, 25 in March, is a former top prospect in the White Sox system who spent the 2026 season with the Orioles organization. He didn’t see the majors, instead suiting up for the Triple-A club in Norfolk all season. The righty-swinging third baseman batted.216/.326/.320 in 100 games and 370 trips to the plate.

That marks three straight seasons with sub-par results at the plate in the upper minors and, more briefly, in occasional big league work. Ramos saw major league time with the 2024-25 ChiSox but totaled only 120 plate appearances. He hit.198/.244/.333 with three homers in that small sample.

While Ramos hasn’t been particularly productive in recent years, he posted big minor league numbers up through the 2023 season. He hit.264/.358/.450 between High-A and Double-A that season but hasn’t produced even average minor league numbers since. Back in the 2023-24 offseason, Baseball America ranked him fourth among White Sox farmhands, calling him a near-MLB-ready option at the hot corner. Even when he struggled through a middling 2024 campaign, Ramos sat 15th among Sox prospects ahead of the 2025 season.

articles.title: Twins To Sign Jose Espada To Minor League Deal
body: The Twins are expected to add right-hander Jose Espada on a minor league agreement, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post. Espada spent last season with the Orioles. He’s represented by The MAS Agency.

Espada, not to be confused with former Astros manager Joe Espada, has made three MLB appearances over the past four years. He’s yet to allow a run across five innings. There was a year in Japan mixed in between his stints in the majors. Espada’s lone MLB outing this season came as the extra man for a doubleheader against the Astros in April. He finished off a blowout win with a scoreless ninth inning.

The majority of Espada’s 2026 campaign was spent in Triple-A Norfolk’s bullpen. He had a solid year, tossing 48 2/3 frames with a 2.77 ERA and just over a strikeout per inning. Espada picked up eight saves with the Tides. The main flaw was a 12.7% walk rate. As tends to be the case with veteran relievers who struggle to get a look in the majors, Espada has had decent strikeout numbers but big walk issues.

Espada flashed a solid three-pitch mix at Norfolk. He led with a slider, which he threw more than 40% of the time. He backed it with a four-seamer that sat around 94 mph. Espada also throws a 90 mph splitter. The arsenal has generated a strong swinging-strike rate in the minors, including a 14.2% mark in 2026.

articles.title: Reds Notes: Sal, Elly, Rotation, Coaching Staff
body: Newly minted National League Rookie of the Year Sal Stewart is a clear building block in Cincinnati, but the Reds have yet to approach Stewart about a contract extension, reports Gordon Wittenmyer of the Cincinnati Enquirer. The Reds locked up budding ace Chase Burns on a seven-year, $105MM contract over the summer. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see them try to work something out with Stewart, though his price tag will probably exceed that of Burns — particularly with some hardware under his belt and a chance to earn some more next week, when Silver Slugger winners are announced.

Stewart, 23 next month, split his 2026 season between the infield corners and batted.263/.330/.457 (112 wRC+) with 32 home runs and an MLB-best 115 runs batted in. He walked at a nine percent clip, fanned at a roughly average 22.1% rate and chipped in 15 stolen bases — albeit in less-than-efficient fashion; he attempted 23 steals on the year (65.2% success rate).

The Reds control Stewart for five more seasons. He won’t reach arbitration until the 2028-29 offseason. Most of the recent pre-arb extensions for players with under two years of service have gone to young stars who play more premium defensive positions than Stewart, who played 948 of his 1311 innings at first base.

articles.title: Blue Jays To Meet With Tarik Skubal
body: The race for left-hander Tarik Skubal now includes the Blue Jays. Jon Heyman of the New York Post reports that Toronto is among the clubs meeting with the two-time Cy Young winner. The Blue Jays join the Dodgers, Mets, and Padres as teams known to be sitting down with Skubal and agent Scott Boras. Heyman adds that two other mystery clubs are expected to get meetings as well.

If the Blue Jays win the Skubal sweepstakes, they’d be taking home the top prize on the starting pitcher market for the second straight season. Toronto secured Dylan Cease on a seven-year, $210MM deal last winter. It was easily the biggest contract handed out to a starter, far surpassing the commitments Detroit made to Framber Valdez and Boston to Ranger Suarez. The Cease contract was also a franchise record, which Skubal would likely smash.

The Cease signing continued a steady trend of spending for Toronto. That’s expected to continue this winter. Team president Mark Shapiro told reporters shortly after the end of the season that he didn’t foresee any changes to payroll. “My expectation is we’ll be in a similar area of support and resources,” Shapiro said, relayed by Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet.

The Blue Jays ranked fifth in payroll at the end of the season at $276,327,620, per our Payroll Tracker. They currently sit at $238,704,279, which still ranks fifth. George Springer’s six-year, $150MM deal is now off the books. Shane Bieber, Jameson Taillon, and Max Scherzer all hit free agency. The club also declined Myles Straw’s $8MM option.

articles.title: Astros Name Brad Ausmus Manager
body: The Astros announced that Brad Ausmus has been hired as the club’s manager. Prior to the official announcement, John Granato of ESPN 97.5 Houston reported that Ausmus would be flying to Houston tomorrow to accept the gig, a report confirmed by Brian McTaggart of MLB.com.

The ties between Ausmus and the Astros go way back. During his playing days, he spent ten seasons as an Astro. He suited up for Houston in 1997 and 1998 and then again from 2001 to 2008. In his post-playing days, he has worked as a manager, coach and has done some front office work as well.

Those various post-playing jobs have come with the Padres, Tigers, Angels, Athletics and Yankees but there have been whispers connecting him to the Astros along the way. Astros owner Jim Crane bought the Astros in 2011, after Ausmus had retired, but Crane has a close relationship with Jeff Bagwell. Over the years, Bagwell has been a key advisor to Crane relating to club matters. Bagwell played for the Astros from 1991 to 2005 and therefore shared a clubhouse with Ausmus for many years.

Since Crane bought the team, the Astros have cycled through various managers, hiring Bo Porter, A.J. Hinch, Dusty Baker and Joe Espada. The Ausmus name would often come up when the job was open and he even got connected to the general manager position in Houston a few times but he continued to bounce around to other clubs.

articles.title: Pirates Notes: Keller, Pitching Pursuits, Lineup
body: Pirates righty Mitch Keller saw his season end on Aug. 2 with a teres major strain that wound up being more severe than was originally known. Keller hit the 60-day IL in early August, but it didn’t come out until after the season that he’d suffered a Grade 3 strain, which entailed the teres major muscle completely detaching from the bone. He remarkably did not require surgery.

General manager Ben Cherington said at this week’s GM Meetings that the Bucs have been conducting in-person visits with members of the roster to discuss offseason plans (link via Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette). Keller’s visit revealed the right-hander to be “basically recovered” after more than three months of downtime, per Cherington. He’s resumed throwing from flat ground and is looking at a mostly normal offseason.

Keller said last month that there wasn’t one specific point where he felt the injury take place. He was likely pitching through the injury for some time before it became fully untenable. Keller started the season well, with a 3.64 ERA through his first 11 trips to the mound. Over his next 11 starts, Keller was decimated for a 7.36 ERA. He showed diminished bat-missing ability, worse command, a greater susceptibility to home runs and, eventually, reduced velocity. Keller sat 93.5 mph on his heater for much of the season but dipped to 92.8 mph over his final five starts — including a season-worst 91.9 mph average in his final trip to the mound.

articles.title: Twins Interested In Bringing Back Ryan Jeffers
body: Catcher Ryan Jeffers has less than a week to make a decision on the qualifying offer extended by the Twins. He’s unlikely to accept it, but the club is already working on bringing him back. Minnesota is “‘engaged'” with Jeffers and pursuing a reunion, relays Aaron Gleeman of AaronGleeman.com.

Jeffers was one of the more popular names at the trade deadline, with several catcher-needy teams attempting to acquire him. The Twins held pat on Jeffers and ended up buying at the deadline. They struggled in August, going 10-17 and falling out of the postseason mix.

Jeffers’ pending free agency made him a sensible trade chip, though an injury muddied his situation. The backstop suffered a left hamate bone fracture in mid-May that cost him nearly two months. Jeffers only played 14 games before the deadline. He performed well in that stretch, as he’d done all season.

The 29-year-old Jeffers followed up a strong 2025 campaign with an even better 2026. He slashed.256/.353/.461 with 14 homers across 368 plate appearances. His 128 wRC+ was his best mark since 2023 when he was splitting the role with Christian Vazquez. Jeffers has been a strong defender at times, but he was a slight negative behind the plate in 2026.

It wasn’t a surprise to see the Twins extend the $23.15MM qualifying offer to Jeffers. He’s almost certain to exceed that in free agency. Minnesota will pick up a compensatory pick if he signs elsewhere. Jeffers ranked ninth in our Top 50 Free Agents list. We have him landing a four-year, $75MM deal.

body: The latest episode of the MLB Trade Rumors Podcast is now live on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and wherever you get your podcasts! Make sure you subscribe as well! You can also use the player at this link to listen, if you don’t use Spotify or Apple for podcasts.

articles.title: Phillies, Brian Navarreto Agree To Minor League Deal
