articles.title: Derek Law Elects Free Agency
body: Veteran reliever Derek Law is a free agent, per his MiLB.com transaction tracker. The Diamondbacks designated the right-hander for assignment in mid-September. He passed through waivers and was outrighted to Triple-A. Law is now back on the open market.

Arizona added Law on a minor league deal in January. He was recovering from flexor tendon surgery at the time and wasn’t ready for the start of the regular season. A setback during his rehab assignment pushed Law’s Diamondbacks debut to late August. He allowed a run in his first outing with the club, then ripped off six scoreless appearances.

The 36-year-old Law doesn’t miss many bats, but he throws strikes and keeps the ball in the yard. The righty put together 90 innings of a 2.60 ERA with the Nationals in 2024. He was set to be a key member of the bullpen last season until arm injuries ruined his campaign.

While Law did a nice job keeping runs off the board with Arizona, his velocity was noticeably down. He sat at a career-low 93.2 mph with his fastball. The heater averaged 95.1 mph with Washington. Law’s cutter, typically his primary pitch, was also down about two ticks.

The Diamondbacks were hit hard by injuries in the bullpen. Closer Justin Martinez was sidelined until mid-August. Lefties A.J. Puk and Andrew Saalfrank missed the entire season. Fill-in closer Paul Sewald was DFAed after allowing a dozen homers in 39 innings.

articles.title: Reviewing The Rays, Angels, And Reds Three-Team Trade
body: The three-team deal that sent Josh Lowe to the Angels and Gavin Lux to the Rays over the winter was intriguing, if not season-altering. Los Angeles picked up an everyday outfielder to replace Taylor Ward, who was traded to the Orioles. Tampa Bay landed a Brandon Lowe replacement after sending the second baseman to Pittsburgh.

And then there’s Cincinnati. The Reds got off the $5.525MM owed to Lux in his final year of arbitration. They also picked up reliever Brock Burke from the Angels. It seemed like a fine bit of business, but not a move that would have a major impact on the season. The trade turned out to be a big win for Cincinnati, and pretty convincingly so.

Burke had a decent run with the Rangers after moving to the bullpen in 2022. He struggled in 2024 and was designated for assignment midway through the year. The Angels picked him up for the final six weeks of the season. Burke made the club in 2025 and put up a solid 3.36 ERA over 69 games. He had a year of team control remaining when he was sent to Cincinnati.

The 30-year-old Burke was tremendous in his lone season with the Reds. He delivered a 2.30 ERA across 74 1/3 innings. Burke’s 77 appearances led the National League. He was the club’s top left-handed option with Caleb Ferguson opening the year on the IL, and manager Terry Francona leaned on him early and often.

articles.title: AL Central Notes: Vargas, Tigers Staff, Royals Ballpark
body: White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas has been a major part of the club’s turnaround this season. The former top prospect, along with newcomer Munetaka Murakami, fueled an offense that ranked fifth in scoring during the regular season. Vargas has set career highs in virtually every offensive category.

The breakthrough season almost didn’t happen. Vargas told Scott Merkin of MLB.com this week that he considered leaving baseball after the 2024 campaign. It’s a topic he touched on earlier this season, but he expanded on it in the recent interview with MLB.com.
“I got to the last couple of weeks of that year, I sit with my dad and we actually … it wasn’t the first time talking about not playing,” Vargas said. “It’s just a hard moment.”

Vargas was dealt from the Dodgers to the White Sox at the 2024 trade deadline. He never found his footing in Los Angeles. Vargas hit just.104 in 42 games with Chicago to close the year. He compiled 237 plate appearances of a brutal 47 wRC+ between the two teams.

“It was so easy to stop playing, but I don’t have an answer to what I wanted to do,” Vargas said. “This is what I have done my whole life. I don’t know how to do anything else. So, I think that was the scary part. This is what I’ve done my whole life. This is what I want to continue to do.”

The 2025 season was a step forward. Vargas notched a respectable.717 OPS as an everyday player for the first time. He took a leap this year, launching 33 home runs and driving in 106. Vargas ranked 16th among all qualified hitters with a 134 wRC+. He even chipped in 22 stolen bases.

articles.title: Sam Fuld Declines Offer To Become A’s President Of Baseball Operations
body: Phillies president of business operations Sam Fuld has declined the Athletics’ offer to become the team’s new president of baseball operations, ESPN’s Jeff Passan reports. Fuld’s name surfaced in connection to the A’s job earlier this week, but Fuld has now taken himself out of the running and will stay in Philadelphia.

Nine names have been linked to the A’s job, though Passan (in another post) echoes an earlier report from The Athletic’s Patrick Mooney and Ken Rosenthal stating that Cardinals assistant general manager Rob Cerfolio is expected to stay in St. Louis rather than pursue the top job in Sacramento. Passan describes both Cerfolio and Red Sox assistant GM Taylor Smith as finalists in the search, and it is unclear how many other names were on the Athletics’ short list besides Fuld.

Fuld spent the last of his eight Major League seasons with the Athletics in 2015, and after retiring from playing in 2017, he joined the Phillies organization in November 2017. Beginning as a player information coordinator, Fuld served in that role until he was promoted to the role of general manager in December 2020. This put Fuld behind only PBO Dave Dombrowski on the Phils’ decision-making depth chart, though an interesting twist occurred in 2024 when Fuld took a leave of absence to pursue an MBA at Wharton. Fuld returned as Philadelphia’s president of business operations this year after attaining his degree, and Preston Mattingly has been the GM under Dombrowski over the last two years.

articles.title: Reviewing The Athletics’ Young Hitters
body: The Athletics were hampered by several major injuries to an up-and-coming lineup this season. Nick Kurtz, Brent Rooker, Shea Langeliers, and Tyler Soderstrom all missed significant time. An offense that ranked 12th in scoring in 2025 slipped to 20th in 2026.

The absences in the middle of the order opened up playing time for a handful of inexperienced bats. The A’s got a good look at several players who could contribute in 2027, even when everyone is healthy. Here’s a look at each young hitter and where they might fit in the plans for next season.

Bolte repeated Triple-A to begin the year, but quickly proved too talented for the level. He slashed.348/.418/.658 with a dozen homers and 17 steals across 37 games with Las Vegas. Bolte was promoted for his big-league debut in mid-May. He got off to an uninspiring start, carrying a.690 OPS into the All-Star Break.

The former second-round pick took off over the final two months of the season. Bolte hit.307 with eight homers and nine steals from August on. He scored 37 runs in 52 games as a reliable table setter in the leadoff spot. Bolte sprinted through the finish line of his rookie season with a.945 OPS in September.

Bolte wasn’t just a major contributor with the bat. He also posted 5 Defensive Runs Saved in center field. The strong debut campaign, and particularly the sizzling stretch to close the season, likely earned Bolte the Opening Day gig in center field next year.

articles.title: Pirates Promote Justin Newman To Director Of Amateur Scouting
body: When he met with reporters in late September, Pirates general manager Ben Cherington revealed that he planned to hire a full-time scouting director. Two weeks later, Cherington accomplished his goal. The Pirates have promoted Justin Newman to director of amateur scouting, Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.

Newman, a University of Rochester alumnus, has worked in various positions with the Pirates since he joined their front office in 2017. He had been their director of player analysis since 2025. Newman’s main focus has been on the draft in recent years, according to Beazley. In his new position, the 31-year-old will replace Justin Horowitz, who left last October to become the Nationals’ assistant GM.

Horowitz was only with the Pirates for the 2024 and’25 drafts, but they appear to have struck gold in both years. The Pirates used their first-round picks on shortstop Konnor Griffin (ninth overall) and right-hander Seth Hernandez (sixth) when Horowitz was in the organization. Griffin was so highly regarded as a prospect that he scored a nine-year, $140MM extension last April. He went on to impress as a 20-year-old rookie. Hernandez, also 20, is on the shortlist of the best pitching prospects in baseball.

Between Horowitz’s exit and Newman’s promotion, Pittsburgh relied on assistant GM Kevan Graves to oversee its draft in 2026. With Graves at the helm, the team used the fifth overall selection on former LSU outfielder Derek Curiel. Graves also led the hiring process for the director of amateur scouting job, per Beazley.

articles.title: Paul DePodesta Discusses Rockies’ Pitching Struggles
body: If you want to take a glass-half-full approach with the long-struggling Rockies, they won 15 more games in 2026 than they did last year. If you want to take a glass-half-empty approach, they went 6-18 in September and clinched the majors’ worst record (58-104) for the second straight season. Colorado has lost triple-digit games four years in a row, and the team hasn’t come close to going.500 or better since a 91-72 effort in 2018. The Rockies’ ace that year was left-hander Kyle Freeland, who overcame hitter-friendly Coors Field to finish fourth in National League Cy Young voting.
[RELATED: Rockies Offseason Outlook]

While Freeland is still a Rockie to this day, he has not approached the success he had eight years ago. He was good for 202 1/3 innings of 2.85 ERA ball then, but the soft-tossing 33-year-old just wrapped up a season in which he posted a 6.65 ERA in 135 1/3 frames. Freeland was a major part of a staff that ranked last in the sport in ERA (5.59), and the Rockies’ run prevention issues weren’t limited to Coors Field. They had a better road ERA (5.35; it was 5.83 at home), but they still came in second to last in that category.

Meanwhile, although the Rockies’ offense tied for last in the league in wRC+ (91), only six teams scored more runs. It’s clear pitching was the main culprit for yet another rough season. President of baseball operations Paul DePodesta acknowledged as much at his end-of-season press conference on Tuesday, as Kyle Newman of the Denver Post relays.

articles.title: The Pirates Nailed The Brandon Lowe Trade
body: The Astros went into last offseason in search of rotation depth. The Rays were looking to offload a cumbersome contract (by their standards). Enter the Pirates, who seized the opportunity and came away with a tremendous trade haul.

Pittsburgh landed second baseman Brandon Lowe, left-hander Mason Montgomery, and outfielder Jake Mangum in the three-team deal. The club sent right-hander Mike Burrows to Houston. The Astros routed a pair of prospects (outfielder Jacob Melton, righty Anderson Brito) to the Rays.

While all three players acquired in the swap made an impact for Pittsburgh, Lowe was the headliner. He smashed 35 home runs as a critical piece in a lineup that has lacked thump in recent years. Lowe finished with an.824 OPS, his best mark since his breakout 2021 season.

The Pirates finished sixth in scoring this season. They flirted with the top spot at times over the summer, but faded late as injuries to key bats thinned out the lineup. It was a huge turnaround after the club finished dead last in runs per game in 2025. Pittsburgh had finished in the bottom 10 in scoring every season since 2018. Even that year, the team ranked 20th. It’s been an inept offense for quite some time.

articles.title: Six Players Elect Minor League Free Agency
body: Six known players have elected minor league free agency in the past three days. While Major League free agents hit the open market five days after the end of the World Series, these eligible minor leaguers finished the season on outright assignments, so they’re able to get a head start on free agency. For further reference, these free agent decisions are all listed on the official MLB.com or MiLB.com transactions pages.

The 33-year-old Alexander got recalled and optioned three separate times early in the season and eventually spent most of it with Triple-A Sugar Land. He had a 5.26 ERA in 87 1/3 innings there with a middling 18.5% strikeout rate. He did throw six scoreless innings for Houston on May 19th, but he allowed 19 earned runs in his other 12 1/3 innings this year. The Astros designated him for assignment in late September. Alexander has a 47.5% ground ball rate in parts of three seasons in the Majors, so he’ll latch on somewhere as a depth option.

Formerly a staple of the Nationals’ bullpen, Rainey only tossed seven big league frames for the Tigers this year. He pitched 47 2/3 innings for Triple-A Toledo and was serviceable there, posting a 3.40 ERA with a 32.7% strikeout rate. Walks have been a problem throughout his career, and this year was no exception, as Rainey gave out free passes at a 14.1% clip in Toledo. Detroit designated him for assignment on August 31st and outrighted him two days later.

articles.title: Jose Urquidy Remains Free Agent
body: 5:00pm: Multiple sources, including Antonio Puesán, now report that Urquidy has not signed a deal with the Pirates. It appears it was a mistake in the MLB.com transaction logs. Urquidy remains a free agent.

4:40pm: Veteran righty Jose Urquidy cleared waivers and elected free agency on Wednesday. He didn’t have to wait long to find a new gig. Urquidy is headed back to the Pirates on a minor league deal, per his MLB.com transactions tracker.

The 31-year-old Urquidy first joined Pittsburgh last offseason. He reached a $1.5MM major league agreement with the club and opened the year as the Pirates’ long reliever. Urquidy was sent down just three weeks into the season. He was knocked around for six earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

Pittsburgh designated Urquidy for assignment in late July. He was soon traded to the White Sox. The righty pitched decently in six games with Chicago, but was DFAed again in mid-September. The Phillies scooped him up to provide some length over the final two weeks of the season. After two appearances, Philadelphia DFAed Urquidy last week.

Urquidy posted a 4.95 ERA across 36 1/3 innings in the big leagues. While the results weren’t great, the workload is significant. Injuries limited Urquidy to just 34 1/3 innings between the minors and majors over the previous two years. He tossed 95 2/3 frames in 20 minor league starts this season, giving him 132 innings for the year. It’s the most he’s thrown since tossing a career-high 164 1/3 innings with the Astros in 2022.

articles.title: Mariners Claim Michael Toglia
body: The Mariners have claimed first baseman Michael Toglia off waivers from the Reds, per a team announcement. It wasn’t previously reported that Cincinnati had placed Toglia on waivers. He’d been on the 60-day IL since early September after dislocating his shoulder.

Cincinnati added Toglia on a minor league deal over the winter after Colorado dropped him from the 40-man roster. He had a nice season in Louisville, slashing.273/.373/.547 with 22 dingers in only 402 trips to the plate before being selected to the big league roster in mid-August. It was a short stay on the active roster, however, as Toglia appeared in only 10 games and took just 28 plate appearances before suffering his shoulder injury, which required season-ending surgery.

The 6’5″, 225-pound Toglia is a switch-hitting former first-round pick who was a well-regarded prospect in the Rockies organization but has never made enough contact to sustain a role in the majors. He did log a career-high 458 plate appearances and belt 25 homers back in 2024, but a 32.1% strikeout rate undercut that power and left him with a.218/.311/.456 batting line (99 wRC+). He followed that with a brutal.190/.258/.353 showing in 337 plate appearances the next season, during which his strikeout rate soared north of 39%. That led the Rockies to designate him for assignment and non-tender him last November.

articles.title: Royals Outright Luke Little
body: The Royals assigned left-hander Luke Little outright to Triple-A Omaha, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. The log indicates that Kansas City technically designated him for assignment on Monday, though the team never announced the move.

Kansas City claimed Little off waivers from the Cubs at the beginning of August. He spent the rest of the season in Omaha on an optional assignment. Little was bombed for 21 runs (19 earned) across 11 1/3 frames with the Storm Chasers. He put far too many hitters aboard, walking 12 and hitting four while throwing three wild pitches. Little had also walked almost a batter per inning with the Cubs’ top affiliate earlier in the season. He finished the season with a 7.28 ERA and an untenable 18% walk percentage in 44 Triple-A appearances.

Little has above-average velocity and cuts an imposing on-mound presence at 6’8″ and 220 pounds. He has yet to sync his mechanics enough to consistently find the strike zone. Little has managed a 2.97 ERA across 36 1/3 career big league frames, yet it’s required him to work around a near-18% walk rate. The free passes have led to more runs in the minor leagues. Little has a 4.62 ERA over parts of four Triple-A campaigns.

This is the first career outright assignment for Little, but he has played parts of seven seasons in the minors. That’ll give him the right to elect minor league free agency at the beginning of the offseason. He’ll be out of options next season and is likely to be limited to non-roster invites to camp.

articles.title: 2026-27 Club Option Preview: October Edition
body: The regular season is now done, which means it’s almost time for decisions to be made on contract options. MLBTR looked at the player options last month. Now let’s turn to the club options. For the sake of streamlining this post, mutual options have not been included, as it’s been over a decade since a mutual option has been picked up by both sides.

Jeff McNeil, 2B: $15.75MM club option (Mets responsible for $2MM buyout as part of December trade) The A’s picked up McNeil from the Mets in the offseason. The Mets were mostly looking to dump some salary, while the A’s were hoping to get a veteran utility guy for their young roster. For the most part, that didn’t work out for the A’s. McNeil had a poor season overall, though he was at least trending in the right direction.

On the whole, McNeil stepped to the plate 520 times with a.264/.313/.368 line and 83 wRC+. That splits up as a.226/.290/.302 line and 59 wRC+ in the first half, compared to a.310/.342/.451 slash and 114 wRC+ in the second half. That’s nice momentum but McNeil has still barely been replacement level this year and will turn 35 in April, so the A’s should walk away. Even if they want to bring McNeil back, they should be able to re-sign him for less than the option price.

articles.title: 12 Players Elect Free Agency
body: Now that the season is over, we’ll start seeing several players choose to become minor league free agents. Major League free agents (i.e. players with six-plus years of big league service time) will hit the open market five days after the end of the World Series, but eligible minor leaguers can already start electing free agency.

To qualify, these players must have been all outrighted off their team’s 40-man rosters during the 2026 season without being added back. These players also must have multiple career outrights on their resume, and/or at least three years of Major League service time.

MLB Trade Rumors will offer periodic updates over the coming weeks about many other players hitting the market in this fashion. These free agent decisions are all listed on the official MLB.com or MILB.com transactions pages, for further reference.

articles.title: Royals To Replace Hitting Coach Alec Zumwalt
body: The Royals are planning to replace hitting coach Alec Zumwalt, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. He’s being reassigned within the organization and not fired, however. Zumwalt will continue on in his role as the team’s senior director of hitting performance but apparently won’t be in uniform and working with the big league staff on a daily basis.

Zumwalt has spent more than a decade working with the Royals. The former Braves fourth-rounder (1999) joined the Royals as a scout in 2013 after his minor league playing days ended. Then-Royals GM Dayton Moore was plenty familiar with Zumwalt, having worked in the Braves’ scouting department and front office at the time Atlanta selected him in the draft.

Zumwalt climbed the organizational ladder in Kansas City, moving from advance scout to director of baseball operations and director of player development. The Royals named him the organization’s director of hitting performance following the 2021 season, and by May of 2022 he’d been shifted into the dugout in place of hitting coach Terry Bradshaw, who was let go after the team started the season mired in a dreadful offensive funk.

articles.title: Kirby Yates Retires
body: Veteran right-hander Kirby Yates announced his retirement this afternoon following the Pirates’ 4-3 walk-off loss to the Tigers in Detroit. In a game that featured Justin Verlander’s final career start for the Tigers, the Pirates opted for a bullpen game, and manager Don Kelly gave Yates the nod as the opener. It was the first “start” of his big league career after 517 appearances as a reliever. Yates recorded five outs, including a strikeout of Dillon Dingler, before being lifted for Yohan Ramírez.

“It was good, but this was it …” Yates told reporters after the game (link via SportsNet Pittsburgh). “I don’t have anything left. Let’s put it that way. I’ve been running on fumes for a while. I think it’s just time. It’s felt like it’s been time for a little while now. I think I’ve given this game everything I have, and in return, it’s given me more than I can ever thank it for or imagine.”

Yates signed with the Rays in 2009 as an undrafted free agent. He reached the Majors in 2014 as a 27-year-old and delivered a decent 3.75 earned run average in 36 innings, working off a low-90s fastball and a low-80s slider to strike out 26.9% of opponents. Yates struggled to a 6.13 ERA over the next two years with the Rays and Yankees but found something of a groove with the Padres in 2017. In 61 appearances for the Friars, the righty struck out a dominant 38.5% of opponents against an 8.4% walk rate and a 3.72 ERA. Around that time, Yates began to move away from his slider in favor of a mid-80s splitter, which would later become his signature pitch.

articles.title: Pirates Not Expected To Make Leadership Changes For 2027
body: Pirates GM Ben Cherington discussed his own future along with many other topics as part of a season wrap-up interview with reporters (including the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review’s Kevin Gorman and MLB.com’s Aiden Stephansky) on Saturday. In regards to his status, Cherington said he expects to return for his eighth year in charge in the Bucs’ front office, as owner Bob Nutting hasn’t given Cherington any indication otherwise.

“Every conversation I’ve had with Bob is just about that. ‘How do we keep getting better?’ ‘How do we assess this season when we need to learn from it?’ The progress, the things that need to get better and what can we do about that going forward,” Cherington said. “Everything we’ve done, really over time, is building toward October, and every decision we’ve made — and certainly every decision we made over the last 12 months — was all aimed towards that. I don’t think that changes. That can’t change. We got to go into this offseason focused on that and beat the other teams.”

While only Nutting knows exactly how safe Cherington’s job truly is, the GM is under contract through the end of the 2027 campaign, and it would be a little unusual to see Cherington fired after the Pirates’ best season of his tenure. The 81-79 Pirates can clinch a winning record by beating the Tigers today or tomorrow, which would mark the franchise’s first time over the.500 mark since their 82-win season in 2018. Pittsburgh went 76-86 in both 2023 and 2024, which was the previous highwater mark of the seven-year Cherington rebuild era.

articles.title: Rockies Outright Vimael Machín
body: The Rockies have sent infielder Vimael Machín outright to the Arizona Complex League, per his transactions tracker at MLB.com. He has the right to elect free agency but the log doesn’t indicate whether he will do so or not.

Machín was selected to the roster on September 5 when Willi Castro landed on the injured list. Ten days later, the club decided to recall Braxton Fulford. Machín was optioned as the corresponding move. In between those moves, Machín got into three games and made six plate appearances. He knocked three singles but also struck out twice. A few days later, when Jose Quintana was reinstated from the 60-day IL, Machín was designated for assignment.

It’s unsurprising that no one claimed Machín off waivers, as he’s a 32-year-old depth guy. This is now the fifth season he has taken part in but he has just 379 plate appearances with a tepid.209/.289/.269 line in those. He has experience at all four infield spots but the lack of offense makes it hard for him to get meaningful playing time.

Machín has been outrighted previously in his career. That gives him the right to reject this assignment and elect free agency. Even if he doesn’t exercise that right for some reason, he would qualify for minor league free agency at season’s end as a guy who has appeared in at least seven seasons on the farm.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Colorado Rockies
body: The Rockies have shown a bit of improvement but are still one of the worst teams in the league. They won’t be trying to compete in 2027. The big question of the offseason is how aggressively they will be shopping players from the major league roster.

articles.title: Rockies Reinstate Jose Quintana, Designate Vimael Machín For Assignment
body: The Rockies announced that they have reinstated left-hander Jose Quintana from the 60-day injured list and designated infielder Vimael Machín for assignment. They optioned righty Gabriel Hughes to Triple-A Albuquerque to make room for Quintana on their 28-man roster.

Quintana, who missed nearly four months with a left elbow sprain, will start against the Mariners on Saturday. The well-traveled 37-year-old and longtime innings eater inked a $6MM deal with the Rockies in the offseason, but he has made just nine starts. In his most recent outing, a May 24 loss to the Diamondbacks, he was crushed for six earned runs on six hits in 1 1/3 frames. Overall, Quintana has pitched to a 5.27 ERA with an unappealing 11% strikeout rate and a 9.4% walk rate in 41 frames. With another trip to free agency looming in the offseason, the one-time All-Star will try to end the season on a positive note.

Machín, 32, joined the Rockies on a minor league deal in December and received a promotion to the majors on Sept. 5. He appeared in three games and went 3 for 6, but the former Athletic and Oriole has hit a non-threatening.209/.289/.269 with two home runs in 379 major league plate appearances. While Machín has slashed a far better.288/.367/.438 with a dozen homers and seven steals in 499 PA in Albuquerque this season, his 94 wRC+ indicates his production has still been 6 percent worse than average in the Pacific Coast League.
